questions.text:
A factory produces widgets. It is known that 5% of widgets have a surface defect. A quality checker randomly selects 12 widgets from the production line.

(i) State the conditions for using a binomial distribution to model this situation.
(ii) Calculate the probability that exactly 2 of the 12 widgets have a defect.
(iii) Calculate the probability that at most 1 of the 12 widgets has a defect.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Achievement: (i) Fixed n = 12 trials, two outcomes (defective/not), constant p = 0.05, independent trials.

Step 2: (ii) P(X = 2) = C(12,2) × 0.05² × 0.95¹⁰ = 66 × 0.0025 × 0.5987 = 0.0988.

Step 3: (iii) P(X ≤ 1) = P(0) + P(1).

Step 4: P(0) = 0.95¹² = 0.5404.

Step 5: P(1) = C(12,1) × 0.05 × 0.95¹¹ = 12 × 0.05 × 0.5688 = 0.3413.

Step 6: P(X ≤ 1) = 0.8816.

questions.text:
The factory produces 3,000 widgets per day.

(i) What is the expected number of defective widgets per day?
(ii) Using a normal approximation to the binomial, find the probability that more than 170 widgets are defective on a given day.

The number of visitors entering a library follows a Poisson distribution with a mean of 12 per hour.

(i) Find the probability that exactly 10 visitors enter in a given hour.
(ii) Find the probability that no visitors enter in a 5-minute period.
(iii) The library has seating for 18 visitors at a time. If visitors browse for exactly one hour on average, find the probability that all seats are occupied at any given time.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- (i) P(X = 10) = e⁻¹² × 12¹⁰/10! ≈ 0.1048 (from tables or calculator).
- (ii) In 5 min, λ = 1.
- P(X = 0) = e⁻¹ = 0.3679.

For Merit:
- (iii) P(X ≥ 18) = 1 - P(X ≤ 17) where X ~ Poisson(12).
- Using tables: P(X ≤ 17) ≈ 0.9370, so P(X ≥ 18) ≈ 0.0630.
- About 6.3% of the time all seats would be occupied.

questions.text: The library owner wants to add extra seating so that there are enough seats at least 98% of the time. Using a normal approximation to the Poisson distribution, calculate the minimum number of seats needed.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Excellence: X ~ Poisson(12) ≈ N(12, √12).

Step 2: μ = 12, σ = √12 = 3.464.

Step 3: Need P(X ≤ k) ≥ 0.98.

Step 4: z = 2.054 for 98th percentile.

Step 5: k = 12 + 2.054 × 3.464 = 12 + 7.11 = 19.11.

Step 6: Round up to 20 seats.

Step 7: Must show clear working with the normal approximation.

questions.text:
Three flatmates, Aroha, Te Koha, and Hine, each independently attempt a daily quiz. The probability that Aroha solves it is 0.75, Te Koha is 0.65, and Hine is 0.55.

(i) Find the probability that all three solve the puzzle.
(ii) Find the probability that exactly one of them solves the puzzle.
(iii) Find the probability that at least two of them solve the puzzle.
(iv) Given that exactly two of them solved the puzzle, find the probability that Aroha was one of the two who solved it.
